coalmarch.acq_note: Scorpion acquired Coalmarch Marketing on 2026-10-19; Coalmarch's pest and lawn client book moved under Scorpion's RevenueMAX platform.
coalmarch.template: Drupal 10 on Pantheon with a shared 'sprowt3' theme and a shared GTM-era analytics pattern; the same build recurs across the pest and lawn book.
coalmarch.inherited: The shared sprowt3 Drupal template, the GTM-that-fires-before-any-consent-gate pattern, the Universal-Analytics-id-left-in-container pattern, the Product-schema-on-a-service pattern and the long-title/thin-meta pattern are template-level, so they are inherited from the agency, not owned by the business.

1seo.acq_note: Scorpion acquired 1SEO Digital Agency on 2026-06-18; 1SEO's home-services, legal, health and franchise clients moved onto Scorpion's RevenueMAX platform.
1seo.template: WordPress with Elementor; CallRail call tracking and a Google Ads tag are wired through GTM. Richer schema than the Coalmarch book, but internal linking leaves many sitemap URLs orphaned.
1seo.inherited: The Elementor build, the GTM-mediated CallRail and Google Ads wiring and the orphaned-location-page pattern are template-level; the license numbers and NAP that are correct are owned by the business.

gngf.agency: Get Noticed Get Found / GNGF (now Scorpion)
gngf.acq_note: Scorpion acquired GNGF on 2024-09-18; GNGF was a law-firm-only agency and its clients were offered Scorpion's platform.
gngf.template: WordPress on a GNGF Genesis child theme (the gngf_vars handle is still in the page); some firms have since been migrated onto Scorpion's scorpcloud platform.
gngf.inherited: The Genesis child theme and the GNGF script wiring are inherited; a firm still on the GNGF theme two years after the acquisition is a sign the promised platform migration has not reached it.

scorpion.acq_note: Hosted directly on Scorpion's own scorpcloud platform; a native Scorpion client rather than an acquired one.
scorpion.template: Scorpion scorpcloud platform behind Cloudflare; the roster is one hosting-fingerprint pull away because every client resolves into the scorpcloud CNAME zone.
scorpion.inherited: The whole site is the Scorpion platform; ownership of the site, its CMS and its data sits with Scorpion, not the business, which is the central lock-in the Hit Board names.

americanturfandtreecare.com.headline: A fast, server-rendered Coalmarch lawn-care site that still leaks analytics before consent, mislabels every service as a retail Product, and captures its own name but none of its money searches.
americanturfandtreecare.com.one_rival: The Greeley and Fort Collins lawn-care pack that owns the non-brand 'lawn care greeley / fort collins' autocomplete while American Turf appears only on its own name; that is where the paid and local work has to win ground.
americanturfandtreecare.com.one_paid: No ads.txt and no observable paid tag on the money pages: the site is built for organic and GBP, so a disciplined Local Services Ads and Google Ads test in Greeley, Loveland and Fort Collins is unclaimed ground the incumbent is leaving on the table.
americanturfandtreecare.com.one_exposure: Google Ads, DoubleClick, GA4, Microsoft UET and a call-tracking vendor all fire on load with no consent banner anywhere on the site; for a business that serves customers who can be in California, that pre-consent firing is the one thing that could draw a complaint.
americanturfandtreecare.com.wins: The raw HTML carries the content (0% JS-dependent), lab LCP is under 1s, 30 of 30 crawled pages are indexable, and the location pages carry genuinely unique copy.

soundpestcontrol.com.headline: A Coalmarch pest site whose own sitemap points Google at noindex and redirecting pages, buries 17 titles past the snippet limit, and still runs a 2016 Universal Analytics id in the container.
soundpestcontrol.com.one_rival: The Tacoma and Olympia pest pack that holds the non-brand 'pest control tacoma / olympia' autocomplete; Sound Pest is present only on its own name, so the gap is the whole Puget Sound money term set.
soundpestcontrol.com.one_paid: No observable paid tag: the incumbent is not running or not instrumenting Google Ads or LSA from these pages, so paid search and Local Services Ads across Kitsap and Pierce county are open ground.
soundpestcontrol.com.one_exposure: Chat, Google Ads, GA4 and Microsoft UET fire before any consent gate on every page, with no banner; the sitemap-to-noindex conflict is a Google-hygiene problem, the pre-consent firing is the compliance one.
soundpestcontrol.com.wins: FAQ schema is present and valid on six pages, the raw HTML is server-rendered, and lab LCP is strong.

midwestpest.com.headline: A Coalmarch Omaha pest site that labels every service as a retail Product for the schema engine, runs 27 over-length titles, and keeps a dead 2020 Universal Analytics id firing beside GA4.
midwestpest.com.one_rival: The Omaha and Lincoln pest pack that owns 'pest control omaha / exterminator omaha'; Midwest appears on its brand and on 'pest control lincoln ne' but is absent from the core Omaha money terms.
midwestpest.com.one_paid: No observable paid tag on the money set: Google Ads and LSA across the Omaha metro are unclaimed from these pages.
midwestpest.com.one_exposure: Google Ads, DoubleClick, GA4 and Microsoft UET fire on load with no consent banner; the Product-schema-on-a-service pattern is a GEO and rich-result risk, not a legal one.
midwestpest.com.wins: Server-rendered HTML, the fastest lab LCP in the book (sub-300ms on the Omaha page), and a satisfaction-guarantee that is plainly stated.

henleysplumbingair.com.headline: A richer 1SEO plumbing-and-HVAC build with proper Plumber and HVACBusiness schema and CallRail-instrumented Google Ads, undercut by 17 orphaned pages the internal links never reach.
henleysplumbingair.com.one_rival: The Inland Empire plumbing-and-HVAC pack across Corona, Riverside and Rancho Cucamonga; Henley's has the deepest schema in its book but leaks link equity to orphan pages the rivals consolidate.
henleysplumbingair.com.one_paid: Henley's is the one site in the book visibly running Google Ads (tag AW-17032377429) with CallRail (205364564) attribution, so a landing-page and conversion-tracking read on the live campaign is the highest-value paid move.
henleysplumbingair.com.one_exposure: Google Ads and GA4 fire through GTM on load; the license number is correctly posted, so the exposure is the pre-consent tag firing, not a disclosure gap.
henleysplumbingair.com.wins: The deepest schema in the Scorpion book (Plumber, HVACBusiness, Article, Person, FAQ), a posted license number, correct index/follow directives, and server-rendered content.

arlinghausair.com.headline: An Elementor-heavy 1SEO HVAC, plumbing and electrical build for the Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky market, carrying the weight of a very large page against a three-state service area.
arlinghausair.com.one_rival: The Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky home-services pack; Arlinghaus has the brand and multi-trade breadth but the page weight and template bloat are where a leaner rival wins the mobile race.
arlinghausair.com.one_paid: A paid read depends on the money-page tag stack read in this run; Local Services Ads across Kentucky, Ohio and Indiana is the obvious multi-trade opportunity.
arlinghausair.com.one_exposure: The tag-firing and consent posture read in this run governs the exposure; the multi-state, multi-trade footprint makes license-number display per trade the thing to verify.
arlinghausair.com.wins: Multi-trade, multi-state coverage with per-state phone numbers and a broad service menu.

centercityemergencydentists.com.headline: A 1SEO emergency-dental site for center-city Philadelphia on Elementor with NitroPack, built for same-day and walk-in intent, carried on a single location and a tight money term set.
centercityemergencydentists.com.one_rival: The Philadelphia emergency and walk-in dental pack; the brand term is owned, the generic 'emergency dentist philadelphia' set is the contested ground.
centercityemergencydentists.com.one_paid: Emergency dental is a high-intent paid category; a paid read depends on the tag stack read in this run, and LSA for the dental category plus Google Ads on same-day intent is the play.
centercityemergencydentists.com.one_exposure: A YMYL health site: the tag-firing and consent posture read in this run governs exposure, and any outcome or guarantee language on a medical service needs a second read.
centercityemergencydentists.com.wins: Clear same-day and walk-in positioning, a defined downtown service area, and stated office hours.

russellandlazarus.com.headline: A GNGF personal-injury firm still running the GNGF Genesis child theme more than two years after the acquisition, a sign the promised Scorpion platform migration never reached it.
russellandlazarus.com.one_rival: The Orange County and Newport Beach personal-injury pack; the brand is owned but the generic 'car accident / personal injury lawyer orange county' set is dominated by firms with heavier content and link programs.
russellandlazarus.com.one_paid: Personal injury is the most expensive paid category there is; a paid read depends on the money-page tag stack, and LSA for law plus a disciplined Google Ads cost-per-signed-case program is where the budget lives.
russellandlazarus.com.one_exposure: A law-firm site under state bar advertising rules: the GNGF theme still in place, plus any outcome or specialization language, is the thing to read against the California bar rules and the firm's consent posture.
russellandlazarus.com.wins: A long-established firm (since 1984) with a defined Newport Beach base and clear practice areas.

thebugman.com.headline: A Coalmarch pest site on the same Pantheon edge as the agency, walled behind a WAF to a declared crawler, so the read is the hosting fingerprint and the demand map; the on-page audit is a verify task.
thebugman.com.one_rival: The pest pack in The Bugman's market; the brand owns its autocomplete strongly, which is the asset to defend while the money terms are contested.
thebugman.com.one_paid: Not observable from here: the WAF blocked the page fetch, so the paid read is a verify task on the money pages with a browser session.
thebugman.com.one_exposure: The WAF challenges a declared crawler; if it also challenges Googlebot or answer-engine fetchers, pages can quietly drop from the index and from AI answers. That is the thing to verify first.
thebugman.com.wins: Strong brand presence in autocomplete and a long-tenured domain.

evergreenpc.com.headline: A Coalmarch lawn-and-pest site already migrated onto Scorpion's scorpcloud platform and walled to a declared crawler, so the read is the Scorpion hosting fingerprint and the Apopka demand map.
evergreenpc.com.one_rival: The Apopka and Orlando lawn-and-pest pack; the brand owns 'evergreen lawn and pest' and even 'pest control apopka', but 'pest control orlando' is held by the metro pack.
evergreenpc.com.one_paid: Not observable from here: the WAF blocked the page fetch, so the paid read is a verify task.
evergreenpc.com.one_exposure: The site now lives on a proprietary CMS the business does not control; the on-page tag and consent read is a verify task behind the WAF.
evergreenpc.com.wins: Already on the Scorpion platform (migration done), strong brand and local autocomplete presence.

cheryldavid.com.headline: A GNGF-origin consumer-bankruptcy firm migrated onto Scorpion's scorpcloud platform and now behind Cloudflare, so the read is the hosting fingerprint and the brand demand map.
cheryldavid.com.one_rival: The bankruptcy pack in the firm's market; the brand name is owned in autocomplete but the generic bankruptcy term set is contested.
cheryldavid.com.one_paid: Not observable from here: the WAF blocked the page fetch, so the paid read is a verify task behind a browser session.
cheryldavid.com.one_exposure: Migrated onto a CMS the firm does not control; the bar-advertising and consent read is a verify task on the live pages behind the WAF.
cheryldavid.com.wins: Migrated onto the Scorpion platform and a clearly owned brand term; note the brand name collides in autocomplete with an unrelated TV character, a disambiguation problem for search and AI answers.

overheaddoornorthland.com.headline: A native Scorpion garage-door client in Eagan, MN on the scorpcloud platform behind Cloudflare, walled to a declared crawler, with the roster-defining scorpcloud fingerprint in plain sight.
overheaddoornorthland.com.one_rival: The Twin Cities garage-door and overhead-door pack; the brand owns its name but the generic 'garage door repair' metro terms are the contested set.
overheaddoornorthland.com.one_paid: Not observable from here: the WAF blocked the page fetch, so the paid read is a verify task.
overheaddoornorthland.com.one_exposure: The whole site is Scorpion's proprietary platform, so the business owns neither the CMS nor an easy exit; the on-page read is a verify task behind the WAF.
overheaddoornorthland.com.wins: On the Scorpion platform with a recognizable Overhead Door brand affiliation.
